title: Drag tasks into your own order, or under another task
description: Every row on the task list has a handle beside its checkbox. Drag a task between two rows to put it there, or onto the middle of another task to make it that task's subtask — as many as you like under the same parent.
items: The rows slide out of the way as you drag, the same as the timesheet
Aim at the middle of a row and it lights up with "Make subtask"; aim at its top or bottom edge to move beside it
Dragging a subtask out between two top-level rows makes it an ordinary task again; dragging a task between two subtasks puts it under their parent
The first reorder switches Sort by to the new "Manual (drag)", so the list keeps your order instead of snapping back to due dates
A task stays in its own status group — change the status to move it to another one
Subtasks are still one level deep, and a task that has subtasks cannot become one
The handle only appears on tasks you can edit. From the keyboard: Tab to the handle, Space to pick up, arrows to move, Space to drop
pending: The manual-order migration is written but not yet applied. Until it is, making a subtask by dragging works, but reordering does not save and choosing "Manual (drag)" errors.
